news.title: Xabi Alonso highlights impact of 'very complete modern player' Morgan Rogers
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso described Morgan Rogers as a ‘very complete modern player’ after the England international struck his fourth Chelsea goal in our 5-1 win against Bournemouth. Signed from Aston Villa this summer, Rogers has needed little time to settle into his new surroundings at Stamford Bridge despite undertaking a truncated pre-season after helping the Three Lions finish third at this summer's World Cup. The 24-year-old netted on his Blues debut on the opening weekend against Fulham and has also scored away at Arsenal, in our draw with Hull City and in yesterday’s win over the Cherries. Rogers has also registered four assists in his eight Chelsea appearances. It's a testament to Rogers' fitness that despite his workload over the past year – he has played more than 70 games for club and country since the start of last season – he continues to have a decisive impact in games. That point was made to Alonso after our latest victory, and the Blues manager responded by highlighting Rogers' durability and the strong connections he has already built at Stamford Bridge. 'No, [his form isn't a surprise] because he is young, he’s fresh, he’s strong and he’s quick – he is a very complete modern football player,' explained Alonso in his post-match press conference. 'His availability is also very high and this is very important. He looks fresh and he is enjoying [his football] because he’s a great guy and is connecting very well with his team-mates, and with everyone. 'He is having a great impact on the team and the club.'

news.title: Extended: Chelsea 5-1 Bournemouth
Full match: Chelsea vs Bournemouth
Inside the life of Sjoeke Nusken
news.body_en: Sjoeke Nusken shares her footballing journey and how she likes to spend her time behind the scenes. Could you start by telling us where you grew up and what it was like? I grew up in a city called Hamm, close to Dortmund. It's not a really small town or a big city, but something in between. We had a big house there and a garden with a trampoline, so we played a lot outside. I have three sisters, so there was a lot of chaos! What age did you start playing football? What was the name of your first grassroots team? Who has been the biggest influence on your football career to date? My sister. I started to play football because of her. My mum always took me to her games. And then they were short of players, so the coach asked me if I wanted to join. Then the next day, I was asking my Mum when the next training session was! My sister played for the Germany Under-16 national team. But then she decided she wanted to have more free time so she didn't carry on as a professional. What's been your career highlight to date? Winning an Olympic bronze medal. The celebration with the team afterwards was so nice. My sisters drove all the way to Paris just to be there with me and celebrate. So it was a really nice experience. It still feels unreal when I look at my medal and hold it in my hand. Who are your best friends in football? Noreen Gunnewig, and then at Chelsea, Mayra (Ramirez), Hannah (Hampton) and Livia (Peng). There's also a girl who I shared a room with at school who is one of my best friends. Could you name your top three favourite players of all time? Thomas Muller, Marta and my sister. What do you like to do away from football? How do you switch off? Going for a walk, drinking coffee, stuff like this. And trying to play different sports: padel, tennis and ping-pong. Are you watching any TV series currently?Ride or Die. It's a bit of crime, but it's fun as well. Lucy (Bronze) recommended it to me. If we looked at your Spotify playlist, who's dominating your most-played artists of the year?I listen to a lot of German music. German party music, chill music... English music - a bit of everything, really!What are your top three holiday destinations, either that you’ve been to or want to visit?Fuerteventura, I would say home - because that's far away now - and Tenerife. I went there this summer, and it was really nice. If you had guests over for dinner, what would you cook for them?Sourdough bread. And then maybe a rice bowl or something where I put out some pots with different things in, and everyone can help themselves. Can you tell the fans something they might not know about you?I was in the army. I did my education there because you can get sponsored for playing sport. They support athletes, especially in sports where there isn't a lot of money.  I was there for four years, starting at the age of 19. It was a nice experience because you are really close together with your team, a bit like being here at Chelsea. We did some really crazy things!What's the best piece of advice you've ever received?Enjoy the moment. Finally, what does football mean to you? It means a lot. We get to experience so much, like when we went to Australia and New Zealand in the summer. The whole reason we got to go was because of football. I'm really thankful to have the opportunity to do it.

news.title: Baltimore and Malard make mark in dominant France win
news.body_en: Melvine Malard started and scored and Sandy Baltimore registered an assist as France recorded a dominant 9-0 friendly victory over Latvia, but there was disappointment for Alyssa Thompson and the USWNT against Spain. Malard has made an impressive start to life at Chelsea after joining the Blues from Manchester United in the summer, and she maintained her goalscoring form on the international stage this evening. France established an early two-goal lead after Kadidiatou Diani and Anaele Le Moguedec found the net, and Malard grabbed France's third in the 20th minute. Grace Geyoro, a second from Le Moguedec and a strike from Oceane Hurtre ensured France had effectively secured victory by the half-time interval, at which a raft of changes were made, including the departure of Malard and the introduction of Baltimore. The Blues winger made an impact by creating France's seventh goal of the night, scored by Kelly Gago. Clara Mateo and Marie-Antoinette Katoto also netted in the second period to ensure a dominant final score. Across the Atlantic in Washington, D.C., the United States' friendly against Spain ended in a 2-0 defeat for Blues winger Thompson. The 21-year-old started for the USWNT, but they fell two goals behind after 14 minutes. It was a position from which they couldn't recover and Thompson played 67 minutes before being replaced by Ashley Sanchez. Meanwhile, Becky Spencer started in goal for Jamaica as they recorded a 4-3 victory away at Mexico. The Blues goalkeeper had a hand in her country's final goal, with a raking pass forward beginning an attack that saw Solai Washington convert Jamaica's fourth of the night.

news.title: Match gallery: Blues rack up the goals against Bournemouth
Henderson on his dream home debut and free-kick inspiration
news.body_en: Jordan Henderson explained how Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers were persuaded to hand over free-kick duties for the midfielder to complete his brace against Bournemouth, while praising the defensive focus shown by his team-mates in Saturday’s big win. It was a home debut to remember for Henderson as he made his bow at Stamford Bridge. Having swept in the opening goal inside two minutes, he teed up Rogers for our second moments later and completed the scoring in a 5-1 victory with a pinpoint free-kick. There were also two goals by Joao Pedro as the Blues made an emphatic return to winning ways after the international break, capitalising on yet another fast start to the game as we took our earliest two-goal lead of the Premier League era. ‘It was a good day,’ said Henderson with a smile after the final whistle. ‘It was my home debut so it was a big day for me. ‘So I was delighted to play here. It's been a while since my injury in the summer, so it was it was nice to be here at Stamford Bridge for the first time and play. We put on a good performance and got a good result, which is the main thing. ‘It was a very good start. We always say we want to start well, especially at home, which we did again. We started both halves really well, which is important, and got some good goals. ‘We've got the crowd behind us and it's important to start well, but then you need to be consistent throughout the game and that was the most important thing for me. I felt we were more solid throughout the game defensively, which gives us the platform to go on and score the goals. ‘Then it set us up for the rest of the game. I felt today the concentration, the focus, was very good for the majority of the game. When you do that you're just rewarded in the end.’ We continued our high-scoring start to the season with our attacking trio of Rogers, Palmer and Joao Pedro putting in another impressive performance. They drew praise from Henderson, but it was the work off the ball which was at the forefront of his mind. ‘They're fantastic players, with huge talent, of course,’ he continued. ‘What I was most pleased with today was the work we did and the defensive attitude without the ball. ‘That helps the team and that builds us, gives us a platform then, when we're defending as a team. When we win it back, they're so good on the transition. They can kill any team with the skill, the pace, the power, and they’re clinical in front of goal. ‘I know everyone will speak about the goals and that's what everyone wants to see, of course, but for me I thought they worked outstandingly hard for the team today and that's what I'm most impressed with.’ Henderson also explained how his younger team-mates were persuaded to step aside and hand him free-kick duties against Bournemouth, having worked on set-pieces with coach Austin MacPhee at Cobham during the international break. It certainly paid off as he curled in what Xabi Alonso described as a ‘beauty’. ‘Some of the lads and Austin have a little bit of confidence in me, so when I have some confidence in me, I can step up and take it. But we've been working on it in training for the past week or two, to be fair, and I was pretty consistent. ‘Austin said: "Forget it, that's what we're doing”. Morgs wasn't too happy, but when we got there he said: "Go on then”. Cole said: "Which corner are we celebrating in when you score?!" So I said they wanted the right, then put it in, thankfully. ‘It was nice because it was something that we worked on in training and we executed it really well. So I was thankful for Cole and Morgs to let me have it.’ Next up, the ultimate derby day. news.title: Highlights: Chelsea 5-1 Bournemouth
Alonso on Palmer's new contract: You want to keep the best for years
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says Cole Palmer will be a ‘top-class player for many years’ and expressed his happiness that the 24-year-old has signed a new eight-year contract with the Blues. Palmer has blossomed into one of the world’s finest attacking players since joining the Blues and it was confirmed today that the England international had agreed a new deal until 2034. He followed that announcement by starting against Bournemouth this afternoon and claiming an assist for Jordan Henderson in our 5-1 victory. Following our win, Alonso emphasised the important role Palmer will continue to play in the Blues’ present and future. ‘I am happy for him and very happy for the club as well, and I’m sure the fans are delighted we have Cole for many years,' said Alonso. 'We need to push him and help him and make sure these years have success. We are building and he is important in everything in that. ‘When a player is young, you want to keep the best ones for years. We believe that Cole is going to be a top-class player for many years, so the longer we ensure he is here, the better.’ Next up, the ultimate derby day. news.title: Xabi Alonso on a complete performance and Henderson's 'two beauties'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes Chelsea produced a complete performance against Bournemouth and praised Jordan Henderson's display after the midfielder struck 'two beauties' in our 5-1 win at Stamford Bridge. The Blues returned to action following the three-week international break and made a historically quick start against the Cherries, with Henderson and then Morgan Rogers both scoring inside the opening three minutes. With our earliest two-goal lead in the Premier League era established, Alonso's side took control of the game. Yet it wasn't until a minute into the second period that our third goal arrived - Joao Pedro striking a powerful finish after good work from Pedro Neto. Evanilson pulled a goal back for the visitors, but the Blues showed the right response. Joao Pedro grabbed his second after an excellent Pep Chavarria cross and Henderson then whipped in an expertly taken 25-yard free-kick to round off the scoring. After the disappointment of our display at Brentford before the international window, Alonso was pleased with the performance from his side, which he felt had control and solidity. 'Today was a complete performance,' he said. 'We were in control for most parts of the game, so I’m happy with that. 'We had good stability. In defence, there were a couple of situations in the first half and for eight minutes in the second, after conceding the goal, we were not in control until we made it 4-1. But overall, I'm happy with the control and the performance. 'There are many positives to take into the future and to keep going.' Chelsea have made a habit this season of scoring early goals, and those netted within three minutes against the  Cherries gave us our earliest two-goal lead in Premier League history. Yet Alonso humbly accepted that our impressive starts are not something he has designed. He said: 'We always try to start the game in the right way and with good energy, but I have no explanation and no credit to me. 'It’s never happened to me that in such a short period we score so many early goals, so let’s see if we can keep doing that. But after the goals, many things still have to happen [to make sure of victory].' Henderson's impact during his home Chelsea debut extended beyond the goals he scored, which Alonso emphasised after the game. The Blues manager said of the 36-year-old: 'We signed him for everything and if he’s able to score two beauties as he did today, we're more than happy for him. 'But apart from the goals, he has done many good things. Take away the goals and it was a very good midfield performance, always involved in the actions, giving solutions to the team-mates with the way he plays and how he communicates with the players around, and with Moi [Caicedo]. 'It was important for Moi to play minutes. We were in a situation where we could adjust his load in the first days [after his return to action]. So, a lot of good news from today, and we keep on going.' Next up, the ultimate derby day. Match report: Chelsea 5-1 Bournemouth
news.body_en: Braces from Jordan Henderson and Joao Pedro, plus a goal from Morgan Rogers, ensured the Blues emphatically returned to winning ways as we defeated Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge. On his home Chelsea debut, Henderson produced a decisive moment inside two minutes. Teed up by Cole Palmer, the veteran midfielder whipped a 20-yard shot home via the post. Then, 60 seconds later, he turned provider as Rogers collected a pass from Henderson and curled a shot home. It was the perfect start. The two quick-fire goals enabled us to take control of the contest. There were no further goals in the first half, but our third of the afternoon arrived within a minute of the restart - Joao Pedro drilled a shot into the net after good work from Pedro Neto. Bournemouth pulled a goal back through Evanilson, but it was only a momentary set-back as Joao Pedro netted his second and Henderson then completed a brace of his own with a wonderful 25-yard free kick. Alonso made three alterations to the side that started our last outing at Brentford. Josh Acheampong came into defence for Wesley Fofana, the returning Moises Caicedo started for the first time this season in midfield in place of Valentin Barco, and Joao Pedro came into the front line for Danny Welbeck. A theme in the opening weeks of our season has been early goals. Yet even the most optimistic Blues supporter would not have envisaged a two-goal lead being established within three minutes. The first was a wonderful strike from Henderson, who on his home Chelsea debut whipped an excellent shot across goal that bounced off the post on its way in. Palmer, fresh off signing a new contract, claimed the assist after an impressive run into Bournemouth territory. From the restart, we immediately reclaimed possession and flooded forward. Neto first had an opportunity, denied by Djordje Petrovic, but we kept the ball alive around the Bournemouth box and Henderson clipped a pass to Rogers, who measured his shot into the far corner via a glancing Antonio Silva touch. Just two minutes and 29 seconds were on the clock. We had never been two goals ahead as early in a Premier League game. In a strong position so early, Alonso's side were able to manage the tempo of the opening period. We didn't overcommit players forward but still maintained a threat in the final third. Henderson came closest to extending our advantage in the first half, with a carefully guided shot from the edge of the box which drifted narrowly wide. Bournemouth fashioned chances sporadically. Rayan had the clearest after he was put through on goal, but Emi Martinez produced a smart reaction save and then denied Ryan Christie's rebound attempt. The Cherries forced the Argentinian into another stop late in the half. Silva this time glanced a header toward goal in the Chelsea box and Martinez had to get down well to save. It ensured we went into the break two goals ahead. Our advantage widened within a minute of the restart. Bournemouth clearly had not learned their first-half lesson. Neto was instrumental to the goal as he got the better of Silva on the byline and squared for Joao Pedro, who powered his shot beyond Petrovic. Bournemouth were not done, though, and five minutes later the Cherries pulled a goal back. It came from a near-post corner that caused a goal-mouth scramble following a flick-on. Caicedo attempted to halt the threat, but his clearance struck the foot of Evanilson and the ball ricocheted into the net. The Blues suddenly came under pressure and Bournemouth attempted to capitalise. Yet we stayed composed and saw off the visitors' threat. In the 67th minute, we grabbed our fourth of the game. It was a well-constructed goal as the ball was worked from back to front before Rogers knocked it out to Pep Chavarria. The Spaniard produced an excellent low cross that took out the Bournemouth back line and enabled Joao Pedro to side-foot home. Four quickly became five – and Henderson was on the scoresheet once again. This time it came from a free-kick, won 25 yards out by Palmer, who stood off and watched as the midfielder whipped his attempt over the wall and beyond Petrovic's dive. With the Blues having opened a commanding lead, Alonso turned to his bench. Caicedo and Joao Pedro, who were nursed back to fitness during the international break, headed off. On came Romeo Lavia and summer arrival Marco Palestra, who made his Chelsea debut after recovering from an injury of his own. The time that remained passed without major incident. Estevao Willian and Danny Welbeck were introduced in the latter stages, as was Malo Gusto, but the game was firmly won by that point as Alonso's side coasted to an impressive victory. The Blues are back in action next weekend as we make the trip to the Hill Dickinson Stadium to take on Everton. Kick-off on Merseyside is at 12.30pm. Our next home game comes the following Saturday against Tottenham Hotspur. news.title: Alonso on Caicedo's return and James' absence against Bournemouth
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso is 'really happy' to have Moises Caicedo back in the Chelsea starting XI for this afternoon's Premier League clash with Bournemouth, and has outlined why captain Reece James is absent from today's squad. The Blues return to top-flight action this afternoon following the extended international break, with the Cherries visiting Stamford Bridge in search of their first league win of the campaign. Alonso's side, meanwhile, are looking to get back to winning ways after a disappointing result against Brentford last time out – an ambition boosted by Caicedo's return. The Ecuadorian midfielder has only made one curtailed substitute appearance this term. However, after recovering from injury during the international break, he is now back in the starting XI. Alonso said: 'We are really happy Moi is back in the Premier League. He is a top-class player and we were missing him. Now we need to help him with his feelings on the pitch. The same for Joao [Pedro] as well. This is how we have used the time in the international break.' There is no James in the squad, though, with Alonso explaining: 'Unfortunately, Reece picked up a little injury yesterday, so we’ll see [in the coming days].' Alonso is up against a familiar foe in the dugout this afternoon, with the Spaniard having taken on Marco Rose during his time coaching Bayer Leverkusen in the Bundesliga. Rose has yet to taste a Premier League victory, but Alonso is aware of the qualities sides coached by the German possess. He said: 'Marco is adapting to his new team. I think many of the ideas they were doing before, he has stayed consistent with. He is a smart coach and was intelligent at Leipzig in the times we played against him. So for sure, today will be a tough game.'

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea line up vs Bournemouth

After a three-week pause in action due to the extended international break, we return home this afternoon to face a Cherries side still searching for its first top-flight victory of the season. The Blues, meanwhile, are aiming to get back to winning ways and, with several players having returned to full fitness, Alonso has made a trio of alterations to the team that started at Brentford last time out. Emi Martinez continues in goal and is expected to be protected by a back four of Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix, Levi Colwill and Pep Chavarria. There is a first start this season for Moises Caicedo, who has recovered from injury, and he is set to be partnered in midfield by Jordan Henderson, who makes his Stamford Bridge bow. Cole Palmer, fresh off signing a new contract until 2034, starts in our attack alongside Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro, who returns to the starting XI after missing our trip to Brentford. news.title: Under-18 Premier League Cup report: Chelsea 2-2 Manchester United
news.body_en: The Blues were forced to settle for a point against Manchester United in the Under-18s Premier League Cup, with Heze Grimwade and Andrew Pennie scoring for the Blues in a 2-2 draw. The match came to life in the second period following a quiet opening 45 minutes. A fantastic goal from Grimwade broke the deadlock just before the hour mark, but it was quickly cancelled out by a Yuel Helufu free-kick. Substitute Pennie put the Blues back in front with a composed finish beyond United goalkeeper Charlie Hardy, yet the home side responded five minutes later as Jaume Camacho-Sidos netted. There was no winner in the time that remained, but we stay unbeaten in the competition. Although it was a quiet first half, the Blues enjoyed the better chances. Mathis Eboue came closest when his left-footed strike hit the post after being played through by a well-weighted pass from Isaac McGillvary. Eboue was a real threat down the left flank, beating his marker on numerous occasions before playing a ball inside or taking on the shot himself. Neither side was to get a foothold in the game in the opening exchanges, and Blues goalkeeper Toby Bell wasn’t forced into a save until the 20th minute, stopping a low-driven effort heading towards his bottom-right corner. Despite flashes of brilliance down both wings and through the middle from Chelsea, the game was goalless at the break. We came racing out of the blocks in the second half, with Eboue leading the charge once more and fashioning a half-chance for the Blues. The move started with Riley Ebho, who held onto possession well and found Grimwade down the line. He helped the ball onto McGillvary, who passed to Eboue. He drove toward the byline before playing a dangerous pass across the face of goal. Unfortunately, no blue shirt was there to meet the cross. Our pressure paid off, though, as just before the hour mark, Isaac Badu won a free kick in a promising area, having wriggled inside from the right-hand flank. Grimwade stepped up and produced a spectacular strike into the top left corner to break the deadlock. It was Grimwade's second goal in as many matches in this competition. However, United equalised quickly as Helafu's long-range effort found the back of the net. We responded, though. Pennie was introduced off the bench and made an immediate impact. A long ball was lofted over the top of United’s defence and into Pennie’s path, and he remained composed and guided a finish into the far corner to re-establish Chelsea’s lead. Once again, Manchester United pulled a goal back within five minutes, this time through Camacho-Sidos. The Red Devils midfielder tucked the ball past Bell, and forced the Blues to settle for a draw. The result takes us to four points in Group F, putting us in second position on goal difference. news.title: Cole Palmer signs new Chelsea contract!
news.body_en:
Chelsea Football Club is delighted to announce that Cole Palmer has signed a new contract until 2034.
 Since joining the Blues in August 2023, Palmer has established himself as one of the world’s finest attacking players. He has provided 91 goal contributions in 138 appearances, won the FIFA Club World Cup and UEFA Conference League, while claiming an array of individual awards.  The 24-year-old has also made history on the international stage, becoming only the second England player to score in a European Championship final when he netted against Spain at Euro 2024. 'Chelsea means a lot to me and I think the club is going in the right direction, so I'm delighted to sign and I’m obviously very happy,' Palmer said. 'Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign. 'Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it too.' Palmer produced one of the finest and most memorable debut Chelsea campaigns after joining the club three years ago. He netted 25 goals in the 2023/24 season, six of which came in back-to-back Premier League hat-tricks, and registered 19 assists. Palmer was voted Chelsea’s Player of the Season by supporters in addition to scooping the Players’ Player of the Season honour. There was external recognition, too, with Palmer named Premier League Young Player of the Season and PFA Young Player of the Year. He remained decisive in his second season. There was a hat-trick of assists in a win at Wolverhampton Wanderers before Premier League history was made with a four-goal, first-half haul against Brighton and Hove Albion. And on the biggest stages, Palmer made his mark. He claimed two assists in our UEFA Conference League win over Real Betis, and later in the summer of 2025, scored twice and assisted Joao Pedro in our FIFA Club World Cup final win over Paris Saint-Germain. Last term, there were 14 further goal involvements, including a strike against Bayern Munich in the UEFA Champions League and yet another hat-trick, this time away to Wolves. Palmer has started the season strongly, scoring four goals and providing two assists in our opening seven matches. Everyone at Chelsea is delighted that Cole has extended his time at the club and we look forward to supporting him in the years ahead. Alonso: We must find composure for what’s uncontrollable
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso and Marco Rose, his opposite number at Bournemouth, are both getting their first taste of Premier League management this season. The key learnings are coming thick and fast. It was Rose’s RB Leipzig that ended Bayer Leverkusen’s remarkable 35-game unbeaten run in the Bundesliga - overseen by Alonso - back in 2024. Today the duo will reconvene at Stamford Bridge but in the colours of Chelsea and Bournemouth, having both moved to England over the summer. Rose has noted in his first few weeks with the Cherries that what happens between both boxes in Premier League games can be difficult to manage. That is a sentiment Alonso agrees with from his time at the Bridge so far, although there are still areas his team can improve. ‘There's a moment that you can control, but to have total control of the game is almost impossible,’ said Alonso. ‘To be able to navigate that, even to feel comfortable, even to control or to have your emotional control when the game is not the way you want it, is very important. It takes time to have that composure to go through those moments. ‘It's the first year for Marco in the Premier League, for myself, and we'll have to learn quick, but because the game is so demanding, and because many teams stress you so much without the ball, you need to be able to manage the control and the no control.’ Owing to the lengthy pause while international football took centre stage, it has been a long wait for the Blues to return to action following the defeat at Brentford. Alonso is hopeful the upcoming fixtures prior to the November break will be the moment his team finds greater defensive solidity and, with it, more consistent results. ‘I think a lot about blocks between breaks,’ Alonso explained. ‘Now we have five Premier League games, three home, two away, and we feel that until now, in certain areas, we were not able to build the stability. ‘Now we want to build the stability patterns to repeat things that will give us this platform for the future as well. Until now we have done a few things good, but other things that we have been missing. For sure, the data is there. In defence, we must concede less goals to have better chances to win games.’

news.title: Chelsea vs Bournemouth: All you need to know
news.body_en: Chelsea’s eight-match tour of the capital from the start of the season draws to a close, with club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton previewing the Premier League visit of Bournemouth to Stamford Bridge. This is the second successive top-flight fixture at the Bridge to kick off at 3pm on a Saturday, as elite club football returns following the international break. Both clubs’ managers were appointed in the summer having previously plied their trade in the Bundesliga.  In fact, while in charge of Bayer Leverkusen, Xabi Alonso encountered Marco Rose’s Leipzig six times, winning three and drawing one, the games averaging 3.8 goals per game. The Cherries are winless in five under Rose (two losses and three draws), rising to seven if you include the tail-end of Andoni Iraola’s tenure. Both teams are yet to keep a clean sheet in this campaign and share a goal difference of -2, though the Blues are the league’s joint-third leading scorers. Chelsea are unbeaten in the past three league home games at our west London home, two of them victories and one a draw. The Blues have won four and lost none of our past nine top-flight bites of the Cherries, though each of the last three ended level, including the topsy-turvy 2-2 in this fixture last season. Moises Caicedo has featured only once this term – a curtailed substitute appearance against Brighton & Hove Albion in August – due to injury, but returned to full training during the international break and is available for selection against Bournemouth. ‘Yes, he is ready to go,' Xabi Alonso replied when asked about Caicedo's fitness in his pre-match press conference. 'We have used the time with Moi to get him back fit. He has been training well and he is okay to go.’ Alonso also confirmed that Marco Palestra, who has yet to make his competitive debut for the Blues due to an injury sustained in the final week of pre-season, is in contention to feature against the Cherries. There was also good news on the fitness of Reece James, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro, each of whom had to withdraw from representing England and Brazil, respectively, due to fitness concerns. ‘They have all been able to train, some of them earlier than others – and Marco Palestra as well. That was the plan. We knew that going into Brentford we had some players struggling but they have trained well and are ready to go.’ Chelsea are unbeaten in the past four league games against Bournemouth at the Bridge, evenly split between wins and draws, with two or more Blues goals on each occasion. It was not always like that. The Cherries picked up all the points on three of their first five visits in the Premier League era, including the first in December 2015. The only prior league meeting in London came in March 1989 as Bobby Campbell’s record-breakers were surging back to the top flight after one season in Division Two. Gordon Durie broke the deadlock for the league leaders against Harry Redknapp’s team, before Graham Roberts converted one of his dozen spot-kicks that season. The Blues’ record home win in the Premier League against the Dorset club came on Boxing Day 2016. Three goals – from Pedro, an Eden Hazard penalty and a Steve Cook own goal – clinched a record 12th consecutive victory for Antonio Conte’s future champions. Last season, the corresponding game was a see-saw 2-2 draw, with all the goals coming in a 22-minute first-half salvo from either side. David Brooks scored for the visitors following a long throw, before Palmer equalised from the spot after livewire Estevao Willian was felled. The tables were turned when Enzo Fernandez fired into the top corner for 2-1, but before the half-hour mark Justin Kluivert tapped in from another throw. Since October 2020, Chelsea have won 10 and taken 35 points from the 21 Premier League matches that followed an international break - drawing five and losing six, scoring 31 goals and conceding six. Morgan Rogers could face the team he played 15 times and scored once for on loan in the Championship during the 2021/22 season. Chelsea are unbeaten against Bournemouth since former Blue Scott Parker led them back to the top flight at the end of that season. Only two Premier League players have made more runs with the ball leading to a shot than Rogers and Palmer (both 18). Chelsea are aiming to avoid joining Everton (1994/95) and Derby County (2000/01) in conceding multiple goals over each of the opening six Premier League fixtures. Hull City (18) are the only team to have received more yellow cards than the Cherries (14), who are also the top-flight’s third most-fouled outfit this season. Three of Bournemouth’s four Premier League wins against Chelsea have come away from home, their only clean sheets at Stamford Bridge. news.title: Alonso praises 'generous' Caicedo and highlights Henderson's growing connections
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has underlined the importance of Moises Caicedo to Chelsea’s midfield after confirming the Ecuadorian is fit to face Bournemouth. Caicedo has made only one appearance this season due to injury, but the prolonged pause for international football allowed him to fully recover ahead of the Premier League's return. As a former midfielder, Alonso knows all too well how pivotal the work done in the centre of the pitch is. Our manager detailed the different ways in which Caicedo helps the Blues in that department, while also acknowledging he has room to get even better. ‘With the midfielders, I have a soft spot, and with Moi, for sure,’ Alonso said. ‘We are all happier when we see Moi on the pitch. Not just myself, his team-mates as well. They are happy to see him not just because he’s a great player; everyone loves Moi because of how generous he is with his effort, how much he helps each of the team-mates, and how important he is. ‘He has a very important role in the team because of the balance he gives, because of the many qualities he has, and he's in a moment where he needs to keep growing, to keep learning. ‘I'm really excited about working with him and having him on the pitch and after each game, getting together and seeing the good things, the bad things, to make him feel confident and to make him feel that he's improving his game understanding.’ Our most recent fixture, at Brentford three weeks ago now, was the day Jordan Henderson was handed his Chelsea debut after injury issues of his own. Despite the disappointing result, Henderson didn’t look out of place, and this further break from match action has allowed him to spend more time on the training pitch acclimatising to his team-mates and Alonso’s way of working. ‘He didn't want many days off,’ Alonso said of Henderson’s involvement since the Brentford game. ‘For him it was important to have the feeling of being back on the pitch after missing pre-season, missing the first games, and to feel how his arm was feeling and to have that confidence. ‘It was important to unlock those first minutes on the pitch. That he was playing that tempo, that intensity for 90 minutes, it was good, and I think that now it will be getting better. ‘We need the right players in terms of quality, in terms of personality, and Hendo has great personality, great experience in the league. Now we have had more time with him, he can connect very well with the players.’

news.title: Internationals: England trio victorious, Cuthbert makes return and Blues duo strike
news.body_en: Hannah Hampton, Lauren James and Keira Walsh all started as England established a 3-1 first-leg advantage in their 2027 Women's World Cup first-round play-off tie with Greece, while Blues captain Erin Cuthbert returned to action as Scotland overcame the Czech Republic. The Lionesses travelled to the Pankritio Stadium in Crete knowing a victory would put them in a commanding position in the two-legged tie. Hampton, James and Walsh were included from the off, while Lexi Potter was named among the substitutes. England dominated possession throughout and Sarina Wiegman's side thought they had taken the lead in the 19th minute when James collected a pass in midfield and produced an exquisite 30-yard lob. However, following a VAR review, the goal was disallowed for offside. The opener arrived late in the first half, as a move started by Walsh ended with Georgia Stanway converting from inside the penalty area. Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo then added to the advantage in the second period. Kallisti Brouksair did pull a goal back for Greece with 13 minutes to play, but England are now heavy favourites to progress to the second round of the play-offs ahead of the second leg at the King Power Stadium next Tuesday. Elsewhere, Scotland's 2-0 away win over the Czech Republic included the welcome return to action for Cuthbert, who hadn't featured since suffering a knee injury while on international duty in June. The Blues captain was brought on as a 63rd-minute substitute, and it was shortly after her introduction that Claire Emslie added to Caroline Weir's opener to put Scotland in control in the first leg of their first-round play-off tie. 💙 Good to see you back, @erincuthbert_ #SWNT | #CZESCO pic.twitter.com/iUsHwZrDup It was also a positive night for Veerle Buurman and Wieke Kaptein, as both started in the Netherlands' dominant 8-0 away victory in the first leg of their World Cup qualifying play-off tie against Hungary. Lineth Beerensteyn and Victoria Pelova netted hat-tricks in the win, during which Kaptein completed an hour while Buurman played the full 90 minutes. Sweden and Nathalie Bjorn also celebrated victory in their play-off first leg in Lithuania. The Blues defender played the opening 45 minutes, but it was in the second period Sweden accelerated, eventually running out 5-0 winners and putting themselves firmly in control of the tie. There was a start for Chelsea goalkeeper Livia Peng, although not a clean sheet, as Switzerland recorded a 7-3 away victory in their World Cup qualifying play-off tie with Israel. Geraldine Reuteler put Switzerland ahead and further goals from Iman Beney, Sydney Schertenleib, a brace from Riola Xhemaili, and own goals from Mia Shvill and Itaf Alkisi ensured a comfortable win. Meanwhile, Giulia Dragoni featured as a second-half substitute as Italy recorded a 2-0 away win in their World Cup qualifying play-off against Belarus. Dragoni was introduced just after the hour with the game goalless, but during her time on the pitch Italy struck twice through Martina Piemonte and Elisa Polli to put themselves in command of their tie. Two Blues went head-to-head during a friendly at the Wildparkstadion as Sjoeke Nusken's Germany faced Ellie Carpenter's Australia. Melissa Kossler'sbrace put Germany in front, but in first-half stoppage time, Carpenter exchanged passes and delivered an excellent near-post cross that Sam Kerr – our joint all-time leading goalscorer – headed home. ...but Sjoeke Nüsken seals the match for Germany, 4-2! 🇩🇪 pic.twitter.com/eDOMbFd499 In the second period, Camilla Kuver added a third for Germany, but Australia were given late hope when Holly McNamara netted in stoppage time. However, that was quickly extinguished as, from a corner, Nuksen collected the ball and powered a finish home to mark her 60th appearance for Germany with a goal and ensure victory. Maika Hamano was also in friendly action, and the Blues forward was on the scoresheet as Japan recorded a 5-1 win over Haiti. Hamano netted her country's second goal of the contest, which came in the 33rd minute, before she was replaced at half time.

news.title: Alonso on Acheampong's 'step forward' and Estevao's importance
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has reiterated that Josh Acheampong and Estevao Willian will play important roles for Chelsea as the season progresses, with the development of our Academy graduate and the Brazilian's influence emphasised. The pair have already featured for Chelsea under Alonso this season and impressed for their respective countries during the international break. Acheampong has become a key player in the England Under-21s side, and helped the Young Lions seal qualification for next year’s UEFA European Under-21 Championship with a game to spare. Our Academy graduate has also made six appearances for the Blues this season, and Alonso feels the 20-year-old defender has shown he is ready to compete at the highest level. ‘Josh has played a few games and is ready to play,’ said our manager ahead of Bournemouth's visit to Stamford Bridge tomorrow. ‘I saw he did well with the Under-21s;  I know he didn’t play the last game but he has done well. ‘He has taken a step forward. He is playing more maturely and more aggressively, and is knowing what it takes to compete in the Premier League. ‘He is on that journey as he has great potential and great qualities. He has played and he will play again.’ There was no competitive action for Estevao during the international break, but he featured in all three of the senior Brazil team’s friendlies and claimed a goal and an assist in the final game: a 4-0 win over India. Still only 19 years old, the winger has time on his side. Alonso is carefully handling the teenager after he missed the end of last season and the summer’s FIFA World Cup due to a hamstring injury, but our manager is certain Estevao’s time will come soon. ‘It’s still early in the season, just a few games since we started. Este is feeling much better from the injury; we have seen with Brazil that he has played more. ‘The context is different when he played with the international team than in the Premier League. We know the demands of the Premier League and we know how important Este can be in some games. He will have his moments and more minutes.’ One player who didn’t travel to join up with his national team was Moises Caicedo, who remained at Cobham to continue working on his return to full fitness following injury. Alonso has confirmed the Ecuadorian has been training well and is available for selection when we get back into Premier League action against Bournemouth, potentially providing a big boost for the Blues with his return to the line-up. ‘For sure, any team would miss a player of his quality, his importance, his weight [to the team] and his dynamic. We have missed him for sure and we are happy that we have him back,’ Xabi added. ‘He feels better and we didn’t want to take any risks against Brentford, for example. I did myself against Brighton and after I said, “Xabi, you did this wrong”. Now he feels much better.’

news.title: Training gallery: Final preparations for Bournemouth
Alonso ready for ‘intense’ and ‘demanding’ Bournemouth challenge
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes the Blues have put our extra time at the training ground to good use during the international break to prepare for the difficult challenge he knows we will face when Bournemouth come to Stamford Bridge. After a three-week break due to the new international calendar introduced for 2026/27, the Premier League returns this weekend with Chelsea hosting Bournemouth in a 3pm kick-off on Saturday. The Cherries are winless in the league this season, but their only defeats have come against Manchester City and Liverpool. Bournemouth’s performances have also arguably merited more than the three points they have won, and they showed their threat with a 2-1 victory away at Real Sociedad in their opening UEFA Europa League fixture. Our manager certainly won’t be underestimating Marco Rose’s side and has been using the time off from matches during the international break to prepare. ‘It will be a tough test,’ said Alonso, when asked for his opinion on our next opponents in his pre-match press conference on Friday. ‘It will be so intense, a high-tempo game and very demanding. They have a clear idea of what they do with Marco and previously with Andoni [Iraola]. ‘The core of the team is the same and every time you have to play Bournemouth it’s tough. But we play at home, and we want and need a win. So we are getting ready for tomorrow. ‘We’ve had time for everything, to analyse what we have done in the games and what is coming. We have been working with some players, recovering some players, we’ve used the time properly for that, and getting ready for Bournemouth tomorrow.’ The Blues are looking to get back to winning ways after going into the international break off a defeat at Brentford as the momentum from our strong start to the season took a hit. However, Alonso underlined that it is still a work in progress at this early stage in his tenure, with the most important thing being that the team continues to learn and improve from every game. ‘It’s going to take time. How long? We’ll keep checking,’ Alonso added. ‘We need to keep improving, keep on learning, be in the process to be competitive, be good, learn how to read the moments and adapt to situations. ‘It’s part of the process and the feeling is that from each game we are learning things, but we need to make sure we don’t make the same mistakes again, knowing that each game is tough.’

news.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Bournemouth
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says Moises Caicedo is 'ready to go' against Bournemouth, and there are also positive updates on the fitness of Reece James, Marco Palestra, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. Following the extended international break, which Alonso described as positive for the Blues but 'probably too long', we return to action tomorrow afternoon as Bournemouth visit Stamford Bridge in the Premier League. The three-week gap between fixtures gave Alonso and his coaching and medical staff quality time to work with several players at Cobham, and five members of his squad have recovered from issues that kept them sidelined in the early weeks of the season or out of representing their countries. One of those is Caicedo. The Ecuadorian midfielder has featured only once this term – a curtailed substitute appearance against Brighton and Hove Albion in August – due to injury, but returned to full training during the break and is available for selection against Bournemouth. ‘Yes, he is ready to go,' Alonso replied when asked about Caicedo's fitness. 'We have used the time with Moi to get him back fit. He has been training well and he is okay to go.’ Alonso also confirmed that Marco Palestra, who has yet to make his competitive debut for the Blues due to an injury sustained in the final week of pre-season, is in contention to feature against the Cherries. There was also good news on the fitness of James, Palmer and Joao Pedro, each of whom had to withdraw from representing England and Brazil, respectively, due to fitness concerns. James and Joao Pedro missed our last outing before the international break, away to Brentford, while Alonso admits Palmer was struggling against the Bees. However, the trio have all trained ahead of Bournemouth's visit and could feature. ‘They have all been able to train, some of them earlier than others – and Marco Palestra as well. That was the plan. 'We knew that going into Brentford we had some players struggling but they have trained well and are ready to go.’ On Palmer, Alonso added: 'He has trained the last week and has felt better. We didn’t want to rush because we had the time. What is most important for Cole is to be fully fit and that he enjoys his game and is feeling okay. 'In the Brentford game, we could see he was struggling and for the next part [of the season] we have a good feeling for him and that he is feeling better.’ The only disappointing news to come from Alonso's pre-match press conference was the confirmation that Jamie Gittens, who suffered an ankle injury while representing England Under-21s during the international break, will be ruled out for the foreseeable future. Alonso said: ‘He is not going to be fit for tomorrow; that is the bad news from the international break. He picked up an injury on his ankle and is going to be out for a few weeks.’ There’s still time to secure your seat and watch the Saturday 3pm action live from the best seats in the house with Club Chelsea. news.title: Levi Colwill on his ‘new chapter’ and how the tough times help
news.body_en: Levi Colwill discusses a new chapter in his Chelsea career as part of an exclusive interview in the matchday programme for Saturday’s Premier League fixture against Bournemouth. The homegrown Blues defender missed much of last season through injury and now has a fresh mentality under Xabi Alonso this season. ‘This is a new chapter in my life and I’m feeling good,’ he explains. ‘I’m a different person, I’ve learned so much, but I feel like it’s for the better, and I’m ready to push on. ‘I’ve seen ups, downs, a big injury. I’ve probably been through more than an average player would normally go through in his career already. But it’s all helped me in different ways, made me more experienced and a more mature head than probably most 23-year-olds out there.’ Colwill also talks about the intricacies of playing in a back three, which is fitting in a programme where our Greatest Games feature harks back to the 2016/17 title-winning campaign, when a 3-0 win over Bournemouth made up part of a 13-game winning run after we switched to a 3-4-3 system at the beginning of autumn. Our latest Legacy feature also takes us back to a title-winning recipe, as we look at the impact of Ted Drake on the club, how he took Chelsea from mid-table mediocrity to our first league championship, before struggling to repeat the trick with a young side known as Drake’s Ducklings. Elsewhere, inspired by Moises Caicedo’s outrageous Goal of the Season winner against Bournemouth in May 2024, we’ve picked out our Five Long-Range Stunners for your enjoyment. We also have all the info you need ahead of this weekend’s match, plus columns from Xabi Alonso, Reece James, Sonia Bompastor and our Academy coaches. We have the latest news, stats and facts, plus your messages. Don’t forget to pick up your copy from the programme sellers around Stamford Bridge, or order online from our official publications partner, Reach Sport.

news.title: Chelsea vs Bournemouth: Key statistics and facts
news.body_en: The Premier League returns after a three-week absence when Chelsea host Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon, and we here take a look at all the vital facts and figures ahead of this weekend's fixture. Chelsea head into the sixth round of matches of this Premier League season in tenth place in the table, eight points behind leaders Manchester City. Opponents Bournemouth are 17th with three points from three draws. Chelsea are unbeaten in our past nine Premier League games against Bournemouth (four wins, five draws), with each of the last three ending level. The run began with a 2-2 draw in February 2020. The Cherries last beat us earlier that same season, when Dan Gosling scored a late winner at Stamford Bridge. Last season’s corresponding fixture at the end of December finished 2-2, with our goals coming from Cole Palmer with a penalty and Enzo Fernandez. The sides first met at Stamford Bridge in March 1989, when Chelsea won 2-0 through Gordon Durie's goal and a Graham Roberts penalty. Following four consecutive home Premier League defeats between March and May, Chelsea are now unbeaten in three home matches in the competition (two wins, one draw). Chelsea are the tenth team in Premier League history to both score and concede double figures in their first five matches of the season (10-12). Only once before have we conceded five goals in our first two home league games without losing: 1932/33, when both matches were drawn and we scored and conceded six. According to Premier League figures, Pedro Neto has recorded Chelsea’s highest speed this season, reaching 35.26 km/h against Brighton on 30 August. That ranks sixth-fastest in the division, while Liverpool’s Bradley Barcola leads overall at 35.93 km/h. Having played 101 games, Cole Palmer is one away from scoring 50 goals in the Premier League for the club. Only two players have reached a half century for the Blues in fewer appearances – Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink (84) and Diego Costa (85). In our last game at Brentford, Josh Acheampong made his 50th appearance for Chelsea and Wesley Fofana started his 50th Premier League game for the club. news.title: Analysis: How Bompastor's resilient Blues are working for each other
news.body_en: There’s change in the air at Chelsea. Currently on a run of nine hours without conceding a goal, the players have a new level of resilience and are showing they are tougher than ever. Here's how... Only three goals have been scored against us in our opening nine matches of the campaign. Three of those nine games have been against Manchester United, Arsenal and eight-time Women’s Champions League winners Lyon. Two more were a high-stakes knockout clash against Real Sociedad for a place in this season’s Champions League. Bompastor’s words reinforce the idea of a shift in focus this season. After the 1-0 win against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge, she said: 'We were also really strong in terms of the mental aspect, but also physical aspects: winning the duels and defending the box. ‘To not concede against an Arsenal side who are a strong team with great talent in the attacking line, midfield, the full-backs...everywhere, it's a great result and performance.' And it shows up in our players’ post-match interviews, too. ‘We were ready for the physical fight,’ said Alyssa Thompson after a hard-earned 1-0 win over Champions League newbies Austria Vienna. ‘I feel great with the team that we have, and we know we can put up a fight and play in these physical games.' After the victory over Arsenal, Keira Walsh explained, ‘We can control the ball, and we are also a lot more difficult to beat. We're really tight defending our box now. We know we can play with the ball, but now we can outwork and outfight teams. We do it as a team rather than individuals, and this year, we know we've got each other's backs. We're working for each other.’ The language in these interviews says it all: fighting, working, togetherness, strength. But it’s not just talk. The hard work is showing up in the physical data in key metrics. They may only look like small improvements to the naked eye, but when the margins between the top teams are so fine, they can be the difference between winning and losing. Those numbers represent a mountain of hard work from the team so far this season, and the success of this approach hangs upon every player buying into it. Let's take a look at last season. Our run of six consecutive Women's Super League titles ended with a third-place finish in the league. Of course, our team was still stacked with talent, but that alone would no longer be enough. Opposition sides had figured out they could earn results by playing the underdog role: working to win every single ball. Perhaps they couldn't beat us with talent, but they just might be able to earn something with intensity. Our 1-1 draw with Liverpool last November shows this pattern. The home side made almost double the number of tackles, as well as more interceptions and duels won. They got their reward with a point, one of only 17 they earned after 22 games in 2025/26. It wasn't just the teams lower down the table, either. A trip to the Etihad Stadium in February saw us lose 5-1 to title rivals Manchester City. It's not a game that Blues supporters will want to revisit, but the stats tell the story. It wasn't just about the goals. The home side won more duels and significantly more tackles to earn their scoring opportunities. In the old Champions League group stage format, we could've faced Lyon at home and away, accounting for a third of the points on offer over six matches. This season, we took on our high-level opponents as one of six matches in the new league phase of the competition. That means a point is likely enough, should we win our other games. The timing of the fixture was difficult. Placed in the middle of a four-game run in the space of 11 days, the trip to France also came just three days after our 1-0 win over Arsenal at Stamford Bridge. Our players looked exhausted at the final whistle after that victory in SW6, so it was tough to imagine they'd be able to put in a similar shift against Lyon. But that's exactly what we did, and the table below illustrates how we matched them in every physical metric on their turf on the back of the performance against Arsenal. In comparison, the French champions were playing at home and had no league game to contend with the weekend before. Their previous outing was an 8-0 win against Servette in the Champions League on 23 September - they therefore faced us after a full week's rest. Not only did we fight for our point, but we also recovered quickly as we returned to domestic action on Sunday. We took on a West Ham side determined to stop us, putting all 11 players behind the ball. The result? A 3-0 win. You can read how we did here. We don't know what will transpire results-wise after the international break. But Chelsea supporters can rest easy knowing this team will be giving it their all in every match to come.

news.title: Pep Chavarria: It’s been an incredible start
news.body_en: Pep Chavarria reflects on his first few weeks at Chelsea in this exclusive interview, explaining what it’s like working under Xabi Alonso and playing in the Premier League. There is something fitting about Pep Chavarria finding himself at Chelsea. The 28-year-old was born in Figueres, the Catalan town which was also the birthplace of surrealist artist Salvador Dali, and the journey that has taken him from his hometown club in the fourth tier of Spanish football to Stamford Bridge certainly has something surreal about it. Chavarria did not take the conventional route to the top. He made his senior debut with semi-professional outfit Figueres at 18, worked his way through Spain's football pyramid, and did not play his first La Liga game until he was 24. From there, he spent four seasons with Rayo Vallecano, making 125 appearances and establishing himself as a dynamic, attack-minded full-back. It earned him the biggest move of his career, to Chelsea this summer. Now, having made his Blues debut in August and begun to settle into life in England, Pep is determined to make the most of the opportunity. 'It’s been incredible,' he says when we ask about his first few weeks at Chelsea. 'To arrive at this club, this amazing club, and the welcome from the team-mates was incredible. I'm very happy with it all, with the staff, they bring me a lot of love. 'We have top players who are very competitive and they have a strong mentality. I love this because I am learning. It's a pleasure to play with these types of players because when you play with the best, you can improve.' Moving to a new country can be daunting, but Chavarria has quickly found people around him to help with the transition. One of them is Moises Caicedo, who has taken on an important role as team-mate and teacher as Pep gets to grips with life in England. 'Moi stays with me always, and he is now teaching me English because I need to learn,' Chavarria explains, in his already excellent English. He is taking weekly lessons and is determined to be fluent by the end of the season. Away from Cobham, Chavarria has also begun exploring his new surroundings with family and friends, ticking off some of London's most famous landmarks. 'The first days I was busy with my family and friends. For example, we went to Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, the London Eye. It's an amazing city.' For now, though, home is a short distance from Cobham, allowing him to enjoy a balance between the buzz of London and the quieter surroundings of the Surrey countryside. That proximity to the training ground is perhaps fitting for a player who has built his career on hard work, patience and a relentless desire to improve. If Chavarria's route to Chelsea has been unusual, his playing style appears ideally suited to the challenges the Premier League throws up. He has quickly discovered that the intensity of English football suits him. 'I think that the Premier League now is the best league in the world,' he says. 'It has intensity, a lot of quality, and the players are top. I think for me it's the best league that I can play in, because I'm a player that has a lot of energy, and I love going box-to-box and working for the team. 'In La Liga it's more structured, more tactical,' Chavarria adds. 'And here, players have more quality and are more physical. ‘It’s more difficult here because all teams have very good players. The last team in the table can win against the first. Because you play against top players, you need to be at your best level, because here, if you don't stay focused, in one second you can lose the game. You need to be very concentrated all the time.' Another familiar element marks Pep's journey at Chelsea. Like Chavarria, Xabi Alonso's senior career began away from the top level of Spanish football, with the future World Cup and European Championship winner starting in the country's second tier with Real Sociedad B, before establishing himself among the game's elite. Now, the pair are working together at Chelsea, with Alonso looking to harness the qualities that helped Chavarria make his way to Stamford Bridge. 'Xabi is one of the best coaches in the world right now,' says Pep. 'I am learning a lot and I know that he wants to help me. Now I am learning and my adaptation is very good. I think that I can do more and I can improve. 'He wants me to attack and defend with a lot of energy. And we have a lot of solutions. I think that we have a team that is very complete.' For a player who grew up dreaming of reaching the highest level, pulling on the Chelsea shirt at Stamford Bridge has inevitably been a special experience. Pep made his first appearance for us away at Fulham before starting the Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town, where he experienced the unique atmosphere inside the Bridge. 'The stadium is incredible,' he says. 'I saw a lot of matches on TV when I was a kid. I remember that and now I say: "Wow, I'm here". You really feel the energy and the atmosphere. 'The fans are incredible and I am very happy because I see them all and I say: "Wow". The shirt, the stadium, all is incredible, and it's so nice. There is an understandable sense of pride in how far Chavarria has come. He has played at every level of the Spanish football pyramid, earned his opportunity in La Liga with Rayo and helped the club reach a European final before making the leap to Chelsea. His career has been built on grit and persistence, rising through the ranks rather than coming through an academy, as is so often the case these days. All of that has helped him grow in character and stature and landed him at the home of the world champions. Now he is determined to ensure the story keeps moving upward. 'I want to win trophies. This is my goal,' he says. 'And I would like to qualify for the Champions League. 'Chelsea is one of the best clubs in the world and always needs to win one trophy per year and play in the Champions League.' He also has a personal target that has long been beyond his reach, but is now firmly within sight. 'First of all, win a trophy, and then go with the national team,’ he says, before adding in a sign of his team ethic and maturity: ‘But for me, the most important is the club.' For a player who had to climb every step of Spanish football to get here, a place in the Spain squad would represent another remarkable milestone. But Pep knows that the route to that next dream begins with what he does in blue. 'I think that we will bring victories and the fans will be happy - happy to win some trophies.' From Figueres to Olot, Zaragoza and Rayo Vallecano, Chavarria has already proved that patience, determination and hard work can take him a long way. Now, in the surreal setting of Stamford Bridge, the latest chapter of that journey is only just beginning.

news.title: Chelsea Goal of the Month winner for September revealed!
news.body_en: Morgan Rogers' brilliant strike against Arsenal has won Chelsea's September Goal of the Month award. The England international opened the scoring inside two minutes at the Emirates Stadium, meeting Jorrel Hato's header from a Reece James free-kick with a first-time finish into the bottom corner. Rogers hit the ball first-time flush on the volley beyond the despairing David Raya in the Arsenal goal to give us the perfect start in north London. Our No.17’s strike was the most popular among Blues fans, receiving 31 per cent of all votes cast. Cole Palmer's fine finish against Leeds United finished second with 25 per cent, while Joao Pedro's effort against Hull City took third place with 19 per cent.

news.title: Lucy Bronze withdraws from England camp with minor injury
news.body_en: Lucy Bronze will return to Chelsea from England duty to manage a minor injury sustained in league action last weekend. The Blues recorded a 3-0 win over West Ham in the Women’s Super League on Sunday, and Bronze played the full match as captain of the side. Bronze has earned 148 caps for the Lionesses and won back-to-back European Championships in 2022 and 2025. She will now not be involved in this window, when England play Greece in a two-legged World Cup qualifier.

news.title: Chelsea FC announces new global partnership with GAC
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club today announces a global partnership with GAC – one of the world’s fastest growing global automotive businesses – which sees the company become the men’s team Official Automotive Partner. The partnership brings together Chelsea’s global football community and GAC’s growing global automotive business, creating closer connections with fans and consumers in the UK, across Europe and beyond. Chelsea FC has one of the largest global fan bases in the world with millions of supporters across Europe and beyond. GAC is one of China’s largest automobile manufacturers and the partnership comes at a time when GAC is expanding its global reach into new markets with its range of high-quality, practical models. GAC and Chelsea first joined forces for the 2026 pre-season tour and this new chapter together will see vehicles from GAC’s AION range escorting the men’s team to Stamford Bridge on selected matchdays. We will also collaborate on digital storytelling, fan experiences and engagement including car displays, providing opportunities for the Chelsea family to discover GAC and its vehicles. The UK and Europe are important markets in GAC’s international development. The partnership with Chelsea adds a new dimension to this work, complementing product introductions, sales-channel development and customer support. It will help GAC reach audiences beyond traditional automotive channels as the company continues to build its presence across the region. GAC’s European line-up includes the AION V electric SUV and the AION UT compact electric hatchback, offering options for family travel and everyday mobility. Both models reflect the company’s focus on practical usability, technology and quality. The partnership also forms part of GAC’s One GAC 2.0 global strategy and its Local for Local approach. By combining the partnership’s international reach with activities shaped around local interests, GAC and Chelsea will build lasting connections together with supporters and customers.
